transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-25
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~50 minutes
Attendees: Evan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Lena (Terraforge Head of ML), Marcus (Platform), Asha (PM)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial):
- Reviewed latest pilot scorecard: overall pass rate up from 86% to 90% on dev set after prompt pruning; regression spikes remain on NER edge cases and numeric normalization.
- Discussed rollback and fallback playbooks; Terraforge wants a staged rollback drill to validate canary policies and VPC fallback.
- Action items assigned for regression run, staging provisioning, and update of scoring sheet.

Topics: scoring thresholds, prompt set v2, guardrail false-positive tuning, rollback/fallback dry-run, SOC2/SSO mention, cost vs latency tradeoffs.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Evan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have about fifty minutes. starting off quick status — Priya you wanna give the summary of the last 48 hours on the evals?
[00:18] Priya: yeah sure, um, so we ran the v2 prompt pruning overnight, it's — it's looking better on the aggregated metric. on the dev set aggregated accuracy moved from 86.1 to 90.3, like evan said. most of the gain's from collapsing redundant instruction templates and tightening the few-shot examples.
[00:35] Lena: that matches what Marcus saw in the staging traces, fewer long tails where the model would hallucinate extra steps. but we're still seeing this recurring numeric formatting issue for invoice amounts — the model sometimes writes "one thousand dollar" instead of "1,000" and that breaks downstream parsers.
[00:50] Marcus: yeah that one we flagged, and it's weird because it only happens when the context includes trailing tokens like 'due by january' — it's almost a KV cache / prefix problem but, um, not sure.
[01:05] Priya: could be tokenization edge-case, or the model variant fallback path. we tried a quick quantized run and the pattern persisted, so i think it's prompt-signal related more than quantization.
[01:18] Asha: is that something the guardrails can catch? we want to avoid bad amounts hitting the downstream pipeline.
[01:24] Priya: yep — we put a numeric-normalizer as post-check, but that increases latency. alternative is to force structured output or a stricter scoring filter that rejects non-normalized outputs. tradeoff is throughput and cost.
[01:40] Evan: right. and for Terraforge's SLA the latency bucket is important — you guys called out 200–300ms p50 for the UX interactions, right?
[01:48] Lena: ideally below 300ms. p95 can be higher but we want predictable tail for billing conversion flows.
[01:56] Evan: ok so two knobs: scoring filter to reduce bad parses (which may increase false rejections) and structured-output enforcement (adds latency). i can update the cost table mapping seconds -> cost hit so you can see the delta.
[02:10] Priya: on the regression side, i ran the top-500 prompt set across the new guardrail rules and found ~12 flake cases where a small context permutation flips label. i put the failures in the sheet under the "failures/flake" tab.
[02:25] Marcus: nice. can you also include the raw request/response pairs? we want to replay them in our staging cluster to see whether it's systematic to our infra.
[02:33] Priya: will do. note: some of the speaker names in the exports got munged — the fireflies export labeled us Speaker 2 etc, sorry about that.
[02:42] Lena: no worries.
[02:45] Evan: switching gears — rollback/fallback. last week we talked about automatic fallback to a compact model for spikes and then to regional fallback. today Terraforge wants a drill to validate the playbook end-to-end. Marcus, what infra do you need?
[02:58] Marcus: we need a staging VPC with a simulated traffic generator and the same routing rules. ideally an isolated node that can capture requests hitting the cache boundary so we can see when the KV cache evicts. also need RBAC tokens same as prod.
[03:13] Asha: and we also want the canary policy that will roll forward minimal requests for 10 minutes and then cut to the older model if errors > threshold — is that supported now?
[03:22] Priya: yes. Redwood's rollout supports canary percentages and automatic fallback when error-rate or latency thresholds are exceeded. there's a policy DSL; i can send an example.
[03:31] Evan: Priya will send the rollout policy snippets + a sample rollback command. i'll also put in the runbook steps for the drill.
[03:38] Lena: on security, we need to confirm that audit logs for request payloads are retained in your private offering for 90 days and that logs can be forwarded to our SIEM. also KMS integration.
[03:49] Evan: yes, for Private we support KMS/HSM, and we can forward syslog or S3 event logs to your SIEM. i will attach SOC2 docs and the audit-log retention page.
[03:58] Marcus: what about SSO/SAML? we need RBAC mapping so our engineers don't get full admin on the cluster.
[04:05] Priya: SSO is available; we support SAML and OIDC. RBAC roles map to the console and API tokens. some of the older exports might say "Redwood Dedicated" as "Redwood ded-uh-cated" in the transcripts, sorry for voice errors.
[04:15] Lena: haha, heard that.
[04:18] Evan: ok, next up prompt scores — Asha, you asked about the thresholds for alpha and beta. can you remind us of the success criteria?
[04:26] Asha: sure. success criteria: 95% correct extraction on top-20 entities, no more than 1 critical failure per 10k requests, and mean latency within 250ms for the customer-facing flow. business will greenlight expansion if those hold for 2 weeks in staging.
[04:39] Priya: based on current runs, we're at 90.3% accuracy overall; the top-20 entities are around 93.5. so close but need the numeric-normalizer fix and a couple prompt templates tweaked.
[04:52] Lena: do you have a recommended prompt surgery?
[04:55] Priya: yes — two small edits: 1) anchor the numeric format in the instruction with explicit examples, 2) add a negative example that demonstrates the reject path. that dropped the flake rate in earlier experiments.
[05:07] Evan: we'll add those edits to v2 prompt set and re-run. priya, estimate turnaround?
[05:12] Priya: i can push the edits and start the regression tonight, results by Monday morning PST.
[05:17] Marcus: for the rollback drill, timeline? we prefer next week in the slot you suggested.
[05:21] Evan: week of Dec 7th? we should schedule a 30-minute dry-run plus 1 hour postmortem. i'll coordinate with your calendar.
[05:29] Asha: please also add a smoke test to ensure no PII leaks during fallback — we need to verify scrubbers still run on compact model.
[05:36] Priya: noted. guardrail team will add a PII-check in the runbook.
[05:40] Evan: quick callout on costs — Luka's cost model earlier indicated the structured-output enforcement costs about +18% on per-token billing due to retries and parsing; using scoring filters instead raised false rejection by ~2% but cost impact was +6%. i will send the updated table.
[05:54] Lena: understanding cost helps product commit.
[05:57] Marcus: one more infra question — if we do Private deployment, can we pin GPU type to avoid variation in latency?
[06:05] Priya: yes, Dedicated and Private give you capacity pinning. you can reserve specific GPU families and memory profiles so kernel selection remains stable.
[06:15] Evan: wrapping up — recap of next steps and owners...
[06:18] Evan: Priya runs regression on v2 prompts and posts details to the sheet by 11/30. Evan to send scoring/cost spreadsheet + SOC2 & audit docs by 11/27. Marcus to spin staging VPC and provisioning for rollback drill by 12/02. Lena to confirm success criteria details by 11/29. schedule rollback dry-run week of 12/07.
[06:40] Asha: that all sounds good. thanks team.
[06:43] Evan: thanks everyone — we'll follow up in email.

End of transcript.
